title: Attention Lab™: The Most Valuable Resource v3.0
description: You cannot make more time or energy, but you can choose where you put your attention. Map distraction, redesign one environment, and test an attention rule for seven days.

measurement.claimsBoundary: Behaviour Evidence Indicators describe source-specific learner evidence. They are not validated psychometric measures, diagnoses, forensic markers or proof of causation.

beiSchema.scoringRule: Record the selected workbook response from 1 to 10 without norming or classification.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: A single learner self-rating; it is not a validated measure of attention capability.

beiSchema.construct: Self-reported frequency of workbook behaviours related to attention
beiSchema.scoringRule: Retain all ten item responses from 1 to 5. A mean may be displayed only when every item is answered and must remain descriptive.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: The item set is not a validated scale and must not be used to diagnose or label a learner.

beiSchema.construct: Learner comparison of a prediction with the revealed story outcome
beiSchema.scoringRule: Record Yes as 1 and No as 0 for this workbook episode only.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: One story prediction is not a general calibration measure.

beiSchema.construct: Confidence in the learner-authored attention equation
beiSchema.scoringRule: Record the selected workbook response from 1 to 10 without norming or classification.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: Confidence does not establish that the learner-authored equation is accurate.

beiSchema.construct: Self-reported areas affected by the selected attention pattern
beiSchema.scoringRule: Retain each selected workbook area as selected or not selected; do not create a risk classification or threshold.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: This is not a clinical, safeguarding, actuarial or organisational risk assessment.

beiSchema.construct: Learner-recorded completion of the selected routine or rule
beiSchema.scoringRule: Count Done responses across seven days and report the observed count as x/7. Missing days remain missing and are not treated as zero.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: The record is learner-entered and does not by itself establish sustained adherence.

beiSchema.scoringRule: Record the selected workbook response from 1 to 10. A difference from BEI-01 may be shown as learner-reported change only.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: A pre/post self-rating difference is not proof that the Lab caused change.

beiSchema.construct: Confidence in the learner-authored attention equation
beiSchema.scoringRule: Record the selected workbook response from 1 to 10. A difference from BEI-04 may be shown as learner-reported change only.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: A confidence difference is not evidence that the equation became more accurate.

beiSchema.scoringRule: Record completion and preserve the private learner-authored text; do not score sentiment or identity.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: Completion does not demonstrate an identity shift.

beiSchema.construct: Learner synthesis of the Attention Lab evidence
beiSchema.scoringRule: Record completion and preserve the private learner-authored summary; no automated profile is generated.
beiSchema.interpretationLimit: The summary is a learner reflection, not a behavioural classification.

### ATTENTION BASELINE — PRE

Before you begin, complete this baseline check-in. Be honest. No one will see this but you.

Each designated workbook response is recorded as a Behaviour Evidence Indicator (BEI): a source-specific evidence point for this Lab.

props.markdown:
### BEI-01: Attention Quality Index (Pre)

"On a scale of 1–10, how good are you at controlling your attention? 1 = my attention controls me. 10 = I control my attention."

### INVESTIGATION 1: THE HOOK

MISSION: Meet someone who discovered what was stealing her attention.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ A prediction about Myah's choice

TIME: 5 minutes

DIFFICULTY:          Observe

### 📖 Read

Episode 1: The Girl Who Couldn't Stop Reaching

Meet Myah.

Myah is fifteen. She carries a notebook everywhere. She writes down what she sees. She has written who she is becoming. She has said it out loud.

But she is running late. Again.

She wakes up, reaches for her phone. Scrolls for twenty minutes. Then rushes to get ready.

Her mother calls from the kitchen: "Myah! Taxi does not wait!"

Same words. Same scramble. Same stress.

That night, she writes in her notebook:

Cue: Wake up Routine: Scroll phone Reward: ??? (I don't even feel good after)

She stares at the page.

She has been tracking her money for months. She has traced supply chains. She has mapped her community's money. But she has never really looked at her own morning. She has never asked herself why she keeps doing something that makes her feel worse.

"What if I changed the routine?" she thinks. "What if I put my phone in the kitchen before bed? Then when I wake up, it is not there. I would have to get up to get it. And by then, maybe I would not want to scroll."

She decides to try. Not because someone told her to. Because she is curious about her own behavior. She wants to see if she can change it.

But she is fifteen. She has written who she is becoming. She has said it out loud. She still does not know if she can change her own behaviour.

The next morning, she wakes up. She reaches for her phone. It is not there.

She lies in bed for a moment. She could get up. She could scroll. She could go back to sleep.

She gets up.

She does not know what she is doing. She just does it.

### INVESTIGATION 3: THE REVELATION

MISSION: Discover the hidden structure of attention.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ Understanding of attention as choice
● ☐ Prediction calibration check

TIME: 3 minutes

DIFFICULTY:           Analyse

### 📖 Read

Episode 2: What Myah Didn't Notice

Myah put her phone in the kitchen. She woke up. She reached for it. It was not there.

She got up. She started her day without scrolling.

She did it again the next day. And the next.

But here is what nobody told her: attention is not a willpower problem. It is an environment problem. You are fighting against a system designed to capture your attention.

Myah changed her environment. She did not try to be more disciplined. She put her phone in the kitchen. That one change—adding friction to the distraction—made the right choice easier and the wrong choice harder.

But she still struggles. She still finds herself reaching for her phone during the day. She still loses focus. She still wonders if she is wasting her attention.

She is fifteen. She changed her morning. But she has not changed everything.

The next day, she walks past the spaza shop. She sees Sipho and Lethabo again. They are building something—a small shelf for the spaza shop. She watches.

"You're the one with the notebook," Sipho says.

She nods.

"What are you building?" Lethabo asks.

She thinks about her notebook. She thinks about her morning. She thinks about her attention.

"I'm trying to build focus," she says.

Sipho and Lethabo look at her. They nod.

"Me too," Sipho says.

"Same," Lethabo says.

She walks home. She does not know if she is building focus. But she is trying.

She is fifteen. She has written who she is becoming. She has said it out loud. She has changed her morning. She still does not know if she can control her attention.

But she is trying.

And something shifted.
